definition: The Mockingboard (a portmanteau between mockingbird and motherboard) is a sound card built by Sweet Micro Systems for the Apple II microcomputers.
details: It provides multiple channels of sound synthesis using one or more AY-3-8910-style sound chips, and some models also offer speech synthesis using Votrax-style speech chips. It improves on the Apple II's limited sound capabilities, as did other Apple II sound cards. Mockingboard cards are supported by many Apple II software products.

explainer.lead: The Mockingboard is a sound card built by Sweet Micro Systems for Apple II microcomputers. It matters because it gave those machines multi-channel sound and, on some models, speech synthesis that the base hardware lacked.

tiers.eli5: It's an add-on board that made an old Apple computer play richer music and even talk.
tiers.practitioner: Retro-computing enthusiasts and developers use Mockingboard cards or emulation to run Apple II software with better audio. The pitfall is that software must be written to target the card, since it is not present in stock machines.
tiers.paperLevel: A sound card providing multiple channels of sound synthesis using one or more AY-3-8910-style sound chips; some models add speech synthesis using Votrax-style speech chips. It improves on the Apple II's limited sound capabilities.

explainer.example: An Apple II game might use the Mockingboard to play multi-channel music and voice clips that the standard hardware could not produce.
